Design review · theedgethatwasnt.com · 8 October 2026

The book site against four publisher and author pages

The site is fast, disciplined and credible, and its dark mode is a finished piece of work. It loses on the thing a book page exists to do: on both phone and desktop you cannot see a price or a buy button without scrolling, and the phone header spends a third of the first screen on eight monospace links that are 17 px tall.

Thirteen pages captured at 1280 px and 390 px (iPhone viewport) in both colour schemes from one headless Chrome, 94 captures in shots/. Scores are 1–5 per criterion on the same nine-criterion rubric as the ThinkDotCo review of 4 October, judged on the home page and the buy path. No site file outside this folder was changed.

28/ 45 · The Edge That Wasn't

Crafting Interpreters 38 · Stripe Press 36 · Pragmatic Bookshelf 31 · No Starch 30 · The Edge That Wasn't 28.

Last in the set, but with the best speed and the best trust story of the five. The gap is concentrated in three criteria that cost one afternoon each: the buy path (2), navigation (2) and imagery (2). R1–R3 below move all three.

The dark-mode question

Yes, what you saw on your phone is the device default. Every page carries the same block: @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { --bg:#161614; --fg:#e8e6e1; … } } (docs/index.html lines 29–35) plus two theme-color metas, one per scheme. There is no toggle, no stored preference and no JavaScript involved: a phone set to dark (or to automatic after sunset) gets the dark site; a phone set to light gets the cream one. The screenshots in this folder were produced by flipping that one media feature and nothing else.

Two things are wrong with it today, and neither is "it exists". The three viewer chart pages (viewer/eur_jpy_indicators.html, eur_gbp_indicators.html, eur_gbp_swing_asi.html) have no dark block at all, so a dark-mode reader who taps "Indicator Viewer" is thrown from a near-black page to a cream one and back. And the experiments explorer's active filter chip paints white text on the mint accent in dark mode at 2.05:1 (the light-mode value #fff was never swapped). Both are token fixes (R4).

Keep automatic, add a two-line toggle, do not go light-only

ThinkDotCo went light-only for a reason that does not transfer: it sells framed art, and a print has to be judged against one wall colour. This site sells a text. Its single image is a cream cover that reads perfectly on either ground, its figures already sit on white panels with a border, and its longest page is a full chapter meant to be read in bed on a phone, which is exactly where dark mode is asked for. The dark tokens pass every contrast check in the appendix (body 14.5:1, muted 6.3:1, accent 8.8:1, button label 8.0:1), so going light-only would throw away finished, correct work to solve a surprise the owner had and no reader will have, since readers chose their own scheme. A toggle costs two lines of CSS selector and ten of JavaScript, lets a reader override the device, and lets the owner check both without touching phone settings. It is a convenience, not a priority, so it sits inside R4 rather than on its own.

The four benchmarks

Chosen for genre, not size: a prestige publisher's title page, two technical publishers' book pages and the best-known single-author technical book site. O'Reilly was attempted and returned "Access Denied" to the headless browser on desktop; it is excluded from the scorecard.

Crafting InterpretersAuthor sitecraftinginterpreters.com · Robert Nystrom. One book, one author, free online text plus print and e-book buy links. The closest analogue: a technical book sold by its own site on the strength of its content.
Stripe PressPublisherpress.stripe.com · The Art of Doing Science and Engineering. Full-bleed 3-D cover, one paragraph, one price. The reference for making a plain cover look like an object.
Pragmatic BookshelfPublisherpragprog.com · Release It! 2nd ed. Cover left, pitch centre, formats and prices right, excerpt and prerequisites tabs. The conventional technical-book page, done competently.
No Starch PressPublishernostarch.com · Algorithmic Thinking 2nd ed. Cover, print and e-book prices with add-to-cart, sale banner. Included as the plain commercial baseline.

How each score was read

First impression
What the first screen says the thing is and what to do. Stripe and Nystrom open on a large cover or illustration and one sentence. Ours opens well (an uppercase kicker, a strong title, the subtitle, the author) but the cover is a 200 px thumbnail and the screen ends on the drop cap; there is no verb anywhere above the fold.
Trust
What a sceptical reader can check. Ours is the strongest story in the set: a public 5,556-row ledger, a broker-reconciled table, four published retractions, a power curve. It loses a point only because none of that is signposted in the first screen; the first trust element a phone reader meets is the −55,000 card, 1,100 px down.
Imagery
Whether the pictures do work. The cover is text on cream, shown small and flat; the same file is reused at 130 px lower down. One figure site-wide on the public pages (the power curve, good). The reference sites either render the cover as an object (Stripe's 3-D jacket, Pragmatic's drop shadow) or lead with an illustration (Nystrom's mountain map).
Typography
One family, a scale, a measure. Georgia system serif throughout with a mono for data is a defensible, zero-cost choice and the hierarchy on the content pages is clear. It loses for three reasons: the measure runs to 88 characters on About and Excerpt, 94 on Ledger and 123 on experiment pages at 1280 px; the mono uppercase eyebrow appears on every page and section; and the five page templates disagree on body size (17, 16, 15 px) and brand weight.
Colour
Cream, ink, one green accent, red for losses; both schemes pass AA on every text pair in the appendix. The one failure is a single chip state and a muted "dead" link colour at 3.4:1. The green-on-cream pairing is less common than the terracotta family and does not read as generated.
Navigation
Eight items plus brand, set in 12.8 px uppercase-ish monospace, wrapping to three rows on a phone: the header is 143 px tall on content pages and 212 px on the explorer and glossary, and every link is 17 px tall, under half the 44 px tap minimum. The viewer chart pages carry a different nine-item nav ("Book", "Charts"). The explorer scrolls a phone past its own search box and list on load.
Buy path
Can a reader buy in one screen. Both ASINs resolve (HTTP 200, paper B0HC5V3YM7, Kindle B0HBT4KW4F) and the JSON-LD offers are correct. But the buy block is the sixth section: on a phone it starts at 3,100 of 6,284 px, after two other call-to-action buttons ("Explore the 81 experiments", "Browse the repository"); the price is never stated above the fold; and the third button, "Read an excerpt", has no style class and renders in browser-default link blue.
Mobile
No horizontal overflow on any page, readable 17 px serif at a 45-character measure, the ledger table scrolls with a hint, the chart viewer folds its toolbar. Loses for the header, the tap targets, and four stacked 150 px number cards that push the first paragraph of explanation to 1,700 px.
Speed
The best in the set by a wide margin: 19 KB of HTML, no web fonts, no JavaScript on content pages, nothing third-party. The only weight is the 304 KB cover PNG (700×1050, drawn at 200 px) and, on the glossary, 154 lazy PNGs at ~2,000 px totalling 8 MB.

What reads templated or machine-made

Fewer tells than most sites of this kind; the palette and the serif are its own. These are the ones a designer would strike in the first pass.

EyebrowsA tracked-out uppercase monospace label sits above the hero ("A MEMOIR OF RETAIL FX, AND WHAT THE RECEIPTS SHOWED"), above the excerpt, as the "INSIDE" heading, as every dt inside the retraction cards and every section heading on 81 experiment pages. Monospace earns its place in the ledger table and the column list on Verify, where it encodes data. Everywhere else it is decoration.
Arrows"→" is appended to six buttons on the home page and to every viewer card title. A button label is a verb; the arrow adds nothing a reader uses.
Card kitThe four headline numbers are four identical rounded cards with the same border, the same radius (10 px) and the same padding, stacked one per row on a phone. The numbers are the best copy on the page; the boxes make them look like a pricing table.
Middle dots"Paperback, 582 pages, $29.99 · Kindle, $9.99", "Every number is checkable · star the repository", the footer line. Each is a sentence that was turned into a meta string.
DriftNot a tell to a reader, but to anyone who reads the source: five copies of the header CSS with different values (muted #615f58 vs #6b6b6b, brand 1rem/700 vs 1.2rem/600, body 17/1.65 vs 16/1.6 vs 15/1.5, nav gap 16 vs 14, footer styled inline). It is what makes every fix below a 95-file edit instead of a one-file edit.

Ten changes, ranked by effect ÷ effort

Effect is the expected movement on the criteria a reader feels. Effort is S (under an hour), M (an afternoon), L (a day or more). Each item gives the problem, the capture that shows it, and the exact change.

  1. Put the price and the buy buttons in the hero

    The page's only job above the fold is to say what the book is and let someone buy it. Today the hero has the title, subtitle and author and nothing to press; the first button a reader reaches (1,500 px on desktop, 2,800 px on a phone) is "Explore the 81 experiments", and the buy block comes after that. Every benchmark puts a price in the first screen.

    Change · index.html
    <!-- inside .herotext, after the byline -->
<p class="price">Paperback $29.99, 582 pages. Kindle $9.99.</p>
<div class="cta hero-cta">
  <a class="btn primary" href="https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HC5V3YM7" rel="noopener">Buy the paperback</a>
  <a class="btn ghost"   href="https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HBT4KW4F" rel="noopener">Kindle edition</a>
  <a class="buy" href="excerpt.html">Read Chapter III free</a>
</div>

/* CSS */
.price{margin-top:14px;font-size:.95rem;color:var(--muted)}
.hero .cta{margin:18px 0 0}
.hero .coverimg{width:240px}            /* was 200 */
@media (max-width:560px){ .hero .coverimg{width:150px;max-width:none} }
/* and demote the lead's two buttons: */
.lead .cta .btn.primary{background:transparent;color:var(--fg);border-color:var(--line)}

    Keep the lower buy section; it becomes the second ask for readers who scrolled. On a phone the buttons then sit at roughly 330–440 px, inside the first screen, with the smaller cover beneath them.

    Effect Effort S
  2. One-row navigation with real tap targets, shared by every page

    Eight 12.8 px monospace links wrap to three rows on a phone, so the header is 143 px on content pages and 212 px on the explorer and glossary, and each link is 17 px tall (measured; the minimum is 44). The viewer chart pages carry a different nine-item list ("Book", "Charts"). The explorer calls detail.scrollIntoView() on first render at ≤760 px, so a phone lands with the search box and list already scrolled off the top (experiments/index.html line 322).

    Change · every header
    nav.sitenav{margin-left:auto;display:flex;gap:2px;overflow-x:auto;scrollbar-width:none;
  -webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch}
nav.sitenav::-webkit-scrollbar{display:none}
nav.sitenav a{flex:0 0 auto;display:inline-flex;align-items:center;min-height:44px;padding:0 10px;
  font:600 .9rem/1 Georgia,'Palatino Linotype',serif;letter-spacing:0;color:var(--muted);
  border-bottom:2px solid transparent;text-decoration:none}
@media (max-width:560px){
  header.sitehdr{flex-wrap:nowrap;flex-direction:column;align-items:stretch;gap:0;padding:10px 0 0}
  header.sitehdr .brand{padding:0 24px 8px}
  nav.sitenav{margin:0;padding:0 16px;border-top:1px solid var(--line)}
}
/* labels: "Indicator Viewer" -> "Viewer"; "Power Curve" -> "Power curve"; use the same 8 on viewer/*.html */
/* experiments/index.html line 322: scroll only on a user's choice */
if(userSelected && matchMedia('(max-width:760px)').matches) detail.scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth'});

    Header drops to about 96 px on a phone, every link becomes a 44 px target, and the nav is one horizontally swipeable row. Do it once in the shared stylesheet from R10, or accept editing the header block in 13 hand-written pages plus the three generators (build_explorer.py, build_glossary.py, the experiment-page template).

    Effect Effort M
  3. Fix the unstyled "Read an excerpt" button

    In the buy block, <a class="btn" href="excerpt.html"> has neither .primary nor .ghost, and index.html has no global a{color} rule, so it renders in the browser's default link blue (purple once visited), bold, with no border, beside two styled buttons. It is the only wrong colour on the site and it is next to the buy button.

    Change · index.html
    <a class="btn ghost" href="excerpt.html">Read an excerpt</a>
/* and a guard so it can never happen again: */
.btn{color:inherit}
    Effect Effort S
  4. Make dark mode consistent, then give it a toggle

    Three faults and one convenience. (a) The three viewer chart pages have no dark token block, so under a dark scheme they render cream while every page around them is near-black. (b) In the explorer, .vbtn.on{color:#fff} was never swapped for dark: white on #5ec89f is 2.05:1. (c) --dead (#8a8880) on the experiment pages' retired-code lines is 3.4:1 on cream, below AA for 13 px text. (d) There is no way for a reader, or the owner, to override the device.

    Change
    /* (a) viewer/eur_jpy_indicators.html, eur_gbp_indicators.html, eur_gbp_swing_asi.html: paste the same block the other pages use */
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark){ :root:not([data-theme="light"]){ --bg:#161614; --fg:#e8e6e1; --muted:#9a988f;
  --card:#201f1c; --line:#37352f; --acc:#5ec89f; --acc-fg:#10231b; --chip:#2a2e2a; --rule:#37352f; --neg:#e08b7d; --pos:#5ec89f } }
/* (b) experiments/index.html */
.vbtn.on{background:var(--acc);color:var(--acc-fg);border-color:var(--acc)}   /* add --acc-fg:#fff / #10231b to its tokens */
/* (c) experiment pages */
:root{--dead:#6f6d66}        /* 4.6:1 on #fafaf8 */
/* (d) toggle: one button in the header, ten lines, remembers the choice */
<button class="theme" type="button" data-theme-toggle aria-label="Switch between light and dark">&#9681;</button>
<script>
(function(){var k='theme',r=document.documentElement,s=null;try{s=localStorage.getItem(k)}catch(e){}
if(s)r.dataset.theme=s;
document.querySelector('[data-theme-toggle]').addEventListener('click',function(){
  var dark=r.dataset.theme?r.dataset.theme==='dark':matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
  r.dataset.theme=dark?'light':'dark';try{localStorage.setItem(k,r.dataset.theme)}catch(e){}});})();
</script>
/* and the selector pattern the toggle needs: the media block guarded with :root:not([data-theme="light"]),
   plus the same tokens repeated under :root[data-theme="dark"] */

    Also note the theme-color metas will not follow a manual toggle; that is acceptable. Figures on the glossary and experiment pages are white PNG panels with a border, which is the right treatment on a dark ground; leave them.

    Effect Effort S alone, M with the toggle on every page
  5. Set the four numbers as a figure strip, not four cards

    The −55,000 / ~$200 / +171 / 4 block is the best thing on the page, and it is wrapped in the generic card kit: four identical rounded boxes that stack one per row on a phone and cost about 600 px of scroll before the first sentence of explanation. Set them as a two-by-two typographic strip with hairline rules and no backgrounds; the numbers carry it.

    Change · index.html
    .numbers{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(2,1fr);gap:0;margin:26px 0 12px;
  border-top:1px solid var(--rule);border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule)}
.num{background:none;border:0;border-radius:0;padding:16px 14px 14px;text-align:left}
.num:nth-child(odd){border-right:1px solid var(--line)}
.num:nth-child(-n+2){border-bottom:1px solid var(--line)}
.num .v{font-size:2.1rem}
@media (max-width:560px){ .numbers{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,1fr)} }   /* was 1fr */
a.num:hover{background:var(--chip)}
    Effect Effort S
  6. Retire the monospace eyebrows and the arrows

    The uppercase tracked monospace label is the one treatment on the site that reads as generated, and it is on every page: the hero kicker, the excerpt source line, "INSIDE", the Verify section headings, every dt in the retraction cards, every section heading on 81 experiment pages. Keep monospace where it is data (the ledger table, code, the CSV column list). Set labels in the body serif. Drop "→" from the six buttons and the three viewer cards; replace the middle-dot strings with sentences.

    Change
    /* index.html */
.kicker{font:italic 1.05rem/1.4 Georgia,serif;letter-spacing:0;text-transform:none;color:var(--muted)}
.inside h2{font:700 1.35rem/1.25 Georgia,serif;text-transform:none;letter-spacing:0;color:var(--fg)}
/* retractions.html */
.retraction dt{font:italic .95rem/1.4 Georgia,serif;letter-spacing:0;text-transform:none;color:var(--muted)}
/* verify.html */
h2{font:700 1.3rem/1.25 Georgia,serif;text-transform:none;letter-spacing:0;color:var(--fg)}
/* experiment template + explorer */
.sec h2,.sec h3{font:700 .95rem/1.3 Georgia,serif;text-transform:none;letter-spacing:0;color:var(--fg)}
/* excerpt.html */
.srcnote{font:italic 1rem/1.5 Georgia,serif;letter-spacing:0;text-transform:none;color:var(--muted)}
/* HTML: remove " &rarr;" from .btn labels and .card h2 .arrow;
   "Get the book — Paperback, 582 pages, $29.99 · Kindle, $9.99" -> "Get the book"
   with the price line from R1 beneath it. */
    Effect Effort S
  7. Cap the measure at 66 characters on every text page

    Measured in the browser at 1280 px: About and Excerpt run 88 characters per line, Ledger 94, the explorer's detail pane 112, and the experiment pages 123 (their main widens to 940 px above 1280). Serif body copy is comfortable to about 75. The phone measure (45) is right; the desktop one is why the long pages feel like a wall.

    Change
    /* about, excerpt, retractions, power-curve, verify */
main{max-width:660px}                       /* was 720 */
/* ledger: keep the table wide, narrow the prose */
main{max-width:860px} main p{max-width:66ch}
/* experiment template: keep figures wide, narrow the text */
@media (min-width:1280px){ main,footer{max-width:940px} }
.sec p,.oneline,.keynum,.meta,h1{max-width:68ch}
/* explorer */
#detail>*:not(.figs){max-width:70ch}
    Effect Effort S
  8. Serve the cover at the size it is drawn, and lighten the glossary figures

    The cover is a 700×1050 PNG at 304 KB, drawn at 200 px (240 on a phone) and again at 130 px; it is the largest contentful paint on the home page and fifteen times the weight of the HTML. The glossary lazy-loads 154 PNGs at about 2,000 px and 300 KB each (8 MB), none with width and height attributes, so the page reflows as they arrive. The OG card (1200×630) is correct as is.

    Change
    # once, from docs/
cwebp -q 82 -resize 480 0 cover.png -o cover-480.webp     # ~25 KB
cwebp -q 82 -resize 960 0 cover.png -o cover-960.webp     # ~70 KB, for 2x screens
for f in experiments/figures/glossary/*.png; do cwebp -q 80 -resize 1280 0 "$f" -o "${f%.png}.webp"; done

<!-- index.html hero (keep cover.png for og:image and JSON-LD) -->
<img class="coverimg" src="cover-480.webp" srcset="cover-480.webp 480w, cover-960.webp 960w"
     sizes="(max-width:560px) 150px, 240px" width="480" height="720" fetchpriority="high" decoding="async"
     alt="Front cover of The Edge That Wasn't">
<!-- build_glossary.py: emit width/height and the webp -->
<img loading="lazy" decoding="async" src="figures/glossary/gen_adx_dmi.webp" width="1280" height="854" alt="…">
    Effect Effort S cover, M glossary (generator change)
  9. Landmarks, a skip link and reduced motion

    Alt text is complete (every img on every page has one, the ledger table has a visually hidden caption, aria-current is set on the current nav item) and focus rings are visible everywhere. What is missing: the explorer and the viewer chart pages have no <main>; the glossary, 404 and viewer chart pages have no <footer>; no page has a skip link, so a keyboard user tabs through nine links on every page; html{scroll-behavior:smooth} and the explorer's smooth scrollIntoView ignore prefers-reduced-motion; the nav has no accessible name.

    Change · every page
    <a class="skip" href="#main">Skip to content</a>   <!-- first child of body -->
<nav class="sitenav" aria-label="Site">…</nav>
<main id="main">…</main>                          <!-- wrap .wrap in the explorer, the chart stack in viewer/* -->
.skip{position:absolute;left:-999px;top:8px;background:var(--acc);color:var(--acc-fg);padding:8px 12px;border-radius:6px}
.skip:focus{left:8px;z-index:10}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){ html{scroll-behavior:auto} .rp{transition:none} }
/* explorer line 322 */
detail.scrollIntoView({behavior: matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches ? 'auto' : 'smooth'});
    Effect Effort S
  10. One shared stylesheet, so the next fix is one edit

    Every page carries its own copy of the tokens, header, nav and footer CSS, and the copies have drifted: --muted is #615f58 on content pages and #6b6b6b on the explorer, glossary and 404; the brand is 1rem/700 on content pages and 1.2rem/600 on the explorer, viewer and 404; body text is 17/1.65, 16/1.6 and 15/1.5 across the templates; nav gap is 16 or 14; the footer is styled inline with a style="" attribute on six pages and placed inside main on the home page and outside it everywhere else. None of this is visible to a reader on one page; all of it is visible across two.

    Change
    docs/site.css          <- tokens (light + dark + [data-theme]), body, header.sitehdr, nav.sitenav, .btn, footer, .skip, focus
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/site.css">   in each page, before its own <style> (page-specific rules stay inline)
build_explorer.py / build_glossary.py / experiment template: emit the same <link> and the same 8-item nav markup
Decide the one value for each drifted token:  --muted:#615f58  body 17px/1.65  brand 1rem/700  nav gap 2px (R2)

    Second-order benefit: the stylesheet caches once across the 95 pages; the 18 KB home page is mostly CSS today.

    Effect Effort M

Typography as measured

Families
Georgia, 'Palatino Linotype', 'Book Antiqua', serif for everything; ui-monospace / Menlo for nav, labels, code and tables. No web fonts, no @font-face: nothing to load, nothing to swap.
Scale
Home: h1 43.2 px (2.7rem), subtitle 20.7, lead 20, body 17/28, numbers 32, labels 13.9, kicker 12.2. Content pages: h1 32 (28 on the excerpt, 24 on experiment pages, 19 on the explorer). Five h1 sizes across the site.
Measure
Phone 40–47 characters per line everywhere. Desktop: home 79, about/excerpt/retractions/power-curve/verify 88, ledger 94, explorer 112, experiment pages 123.
Header
Phone: 143 px (content), 146 (404), 155 (experiment pages), 158 (viewer), 212–213 (explorer, glossary). Desktop 46–92 px.
Tap targets
Nav links 48×17 px on every page except the viewer chart pages (34×29). Buttons 44–48 px tall: fine.

Links and the buy path

  • Live site is byte-identical to the repo's docs/index.html (md5 match); GitHub Pages, HTTP/2, cache-control: max-age=600.
  • Every relative href and src in the 13 reviewed pages resolves to a file on disk; 98 internal URLs fetched from the live site all returned 200, including the 1 MB CSV, the glossary and the three viewer pages. A request for a missing path returns the custom 404 with status 404.
  • Amazon: /dp/B0HC5V3YM7 (paperback) 200, /dp/B0HBT4KW4F (Kindle) 200. JSON-LD on the home page declares both offers with price, currency, availability and the same URLs; ISBN 9798189494147, 582 pages.
  • Repository links return 200; the one blob/main/…csv deep link returned 429 (GitHub rate-limiting the crawler), not a broken link. 416 GitHub code links on experiment pages were not individually fetched.
  • Meta: title, description, canonical, og:title/description/type/url/image/image:alt and twitter:card on every reviewed page; theme-color for both schemes; inline SVG favicon; robots.txt and a sitemap present. No analytics, no cookies, no third-party requests.

What was not changed

Nothing outside docs/design_review_2026-10-08/. The folder holds this page, RECOMMENDATIONS.md (the same ten items in plain text), metrics.json and refs_metrics.json (the measured values quoted above), and shots/ (fold captures as PNG, full-length captures as JPEG, 112 files).

Design review, 8 October 2026. Captures from headless Chrome 151 via the DevTools protocol with Emulation.setEmulatedMedia for the colour scheme and a 390×844 mobile viewport. Rubric and format follow docs/design_review_2026-10-04/REVIEW.html in thinkdotco-site.
